detailed_rationale:
Mphasis Ltd is a mid-tier IT services company specialising in cloud and cognitive solutions, with Blackstone as promoter since 2016 and a client base concentrated in BFSI and 'Direct' (non-DXC) channel relationships. Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) revenue was Rs 4,384 crore with Rs 490 crore net profit (18% operating margin), and return ratios are genuinely solid for the IT services peer set: ROE of 18.5% and ROCE of 22.1%, on an almost debt-free balance sheet. TTM sales growth of 14% and TTM profit growth of 11% are both meaningfully above what the large-cap IT bellwethers (TCS, Infosys) have been delivering through this period of soft global discretionary tech spend, suggesting Mphasis's Direct/BFS-led growth engine is outperforming the sector average right now.

The three-year growth score is low mainly because of the slower 2023-24 period industry-wide (post-pandemic digital-spend normalisation), which the quant model's trailing-3-year window still weighs heavily, even though the more recent trend has clearly reaccelerated -- this looks like the kind of base-period distortion the analyst review is meant to catch and correct for, rather than a genuine current-quality problem. Two watch items are worth flagging honestly: debtor days have risen from 78.6 to 96.4 (one data point, worth monitoring for client-payment stress but not yet alarming), and Blackstone's stake has fallen from over 55% historically to 30.54% -- a long-running, well-understood PE-sponsor monetisation process rather than a fresh distress signal.

Reverse-DCF: a 23.8x P/E for an 18.5% ROE, low-debt IT services business growing revenue at 14% (above sector average currently) is a reasonable, not demanding, valuation -- it does not require heroic growth assumptions to be justified, just a continuation of the current above-peer trajectory. Given the quant model's own one-year score already leans toward Hold (47.8 versus 38.6 for the three-year score) and the fundamentals support that read once the stale 3-year growth base-effect is discounted, I am rescuing this from the quant's overall Sell to a Hold.
recommendation_rationale: Mphasis screens weak on the trailing three-year growth score mainly because of an industry-wide 2023-24 slowdown baked into that window, but the current trend (14% TTM revenue growth, 18.5% ROE, 22.1% ROCE, almost no debt, reasonable 23.8x P/E) is genuinely solid and above IT-sector peers right now. The quant model's own one-year sub-score already points to Hold. I am rescuing the overall Sell to Hold on the strength of the current fundamentals, while flagging rising debtor days as the one item worth continued monitoring.
summary: Mphasis is a well-run, low-debt IT services company with solid returns on capital and revenue growth that is currently outpacing many larger IT peers, at a reasonable valuation. A slower industry-wide period a couple of years ago still weighs on its longer-term growth score, but the recent trend is healthy. We are calling this a Hold, upgrading it from the model's initial Sell signal given the current fundamentals.
positive_para: Mphasis is delivering 14% TTM revenue growth and 18.5% ROE / 22.1% ROCE on an almost debt-free balance sheet, outperforming the growth pace of India's largest IT services bellwethers in the current soft discretionary-tech-spending environment, at a reasonable 23.8x earnings multiple that does not require aggressive assumptions to justify.
negative_para: The three-year growth score is weighed down by an industry-wide slower period in 2023-24 that may understate the current, healthier trajectory, but debtor days have risen from 78.6 to 96.4 -- worth watching for early signs of client-side payment stress -- and Blackstone's promoter stake has continued its long-running decline from over 55% to 30.54%, which, while a well-understood PE-monetisation pattern, does mean a large historical anchor shareholder now owns meaningfully less of the register than before.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A 23.8x P/E for 18.5% ROE and 14% current revenue growth is a reasonable, not demanding, valuation for an IT services business performing above sector average right now; it does not require heroic multi-year growth assumptions, just continuation of the present trajectory. This supports rescuing the name from Sell to Hold.
